Current best source (revision 25aad2bbf5f5b7dff038) key conventions that produced the big gains:
- Declare the 0x64-stride tables as structs so the index scales by 0x64 and gcc emits `andi $v1,$s2,0xffff` + sll/addu chain once per use: `typedef struct { u8 *p; u8 pad[0x60]; } RecP; extern RecP D_8011F350[];` `typedef struct { u16 v; u8 pad[0x62]; } RecS; extern RecS D_8011F32E[];` `typedef struct { u8 b; u8 pad[0x63]; } RecB; extern RecB D_8011F2FD[];`. Plain u8[] + byte index gave the same insns but worse regalloc (8699/6400).
- Keep `arg0` raw (s32) and index with `arg0 & 0xFFFF` inline at each switch store; do NOT hoist `idx = arg0 & 0xFFFF` into a local (hoisting made gcc keep idx in a callee-saved reg and lose the repeated `andi` chain the target has).

- D_8011F4E4 must be an extern u8[] used as `D_8011F4E4 + *(u16*)(*(u8**)(s0+4)+2) * 0x64` so gcc emits lui/addiu into $v1 then `addu $a0,$v0,$v1`.
